title: Positive products and radii of convergence
statement:
Let $\{f_j(t)\}_{j\in J}$ be a locally finite family of series

$$
f_j(t)=1+\sum_{n\ge1}a_{j,n}t^n\in1+t\mathbf R_{\ge0}[[t]],
$$

meaning that each coefficient of the formal product
$F(t):=\prod_{j\in J}f_j(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}A_nt^n$ receives contributions
from only finitely many factors. If this formal series is the Taylor
series at $0$ of a function holomorphic on $|t|<R$, then every
$f_j$ has radius of convergence at least $R$ (in the sense of [d-real-series]). In particular, if
$f_j=P_j(t)^{-1}$ with $P_j(0)=1$ a polynomial, then $P_j$ has no
zero in $|t|<R$.

proof.text: Write $a_{j,0}=1$. Fix $j\in J$ and $n\ge0$. By degreewise local finiteness in [d-real-series], choose a finite subset $S\subset J$ containing $j$ and every factor with a nonzero positive-degree coefficient of degree at most $n$. The coefficient of $t^n$ in $F$ is that in $\prod_{i\in S}f_i$. In the coefficient expansion, the term choosing degree $n$ in factor $j$ and degree zero in every other factor is $a_{j,n}$; all other terms are nonnegative. Thus $0\le a_{j,n}\le A_n$. This also gives $A_n\ge0$ (and $A_0=1$).

Let $h$ be the function in the hypothesis, with Taylor coefficients $A_n=h^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For each real $0\le t<R$, apply [lem-rp-taylor-sum-on-disc] at $c=0$ and $z=t$ to obtain summability of $\sum_n A_nt^n$ in $\mathbf C$. Taking real parts gives summability of the same real series; its terms are nonnegative by step 1. The hypotheses needed by the cited result are exactly holomorphy on $|z|<R$ and $|t|<R$; no regularity on the boundary $|z|=R$ is used.

source.place: ## Proof, analytic convergence input replacing the Cauchy coefficient estimate

proof.text: For every $0\le t<R$ and fixed $j$, step 1 gives $0\le a_{j,n}t^n\le A_nt^n$. Apply [lem-rp-nonnegative-summable-comparison] with $I=\mathbf N$, $u_n=a_{j,n}t^n$, and $v_n=A_nt^n$, summable by step 2. Thus $\sum_n|a_{j,n}|t^n$ converges for every such $t$. By the supremum definition of radius in [d-real-series], $R(f_j)\ge R$. For $R=\infty$ this means convergence at every finite $t\ge0$. If $R=0$, the radius bound is automatic and the disc is empty.

source.place: ## Proof, radius comparison and passage to R

proof.text: For the last assertion write $P=P_j=\sum_{k=0}^d p_kt^k$ and $f_j=\sum_{n\ge0}b_nt^n$ with $b_n=a_{j,n}\ge0$. By the coefficientwise product convention in [d-real-series], $Pf_j=1$ says $\sum_{k=0}^{\min(d,m)}p_kb_{m-k}=\delta_{m,0}$. Put $s_N(z)=\sum_{n=0}^N b_nz^n$. For $N\ge d$, multiply these coefficient equations by $z^m$ and sum over $0\le m\le N$. Rearranging this finite sum gives $1=\sum_{k=0}^d p_kz^k s_{N-k}(z)$.

source.place: ## Proof, last sentence: expand the inverse-polynomial identity

proof.text: Suppose $P(z)=0$ with $|z|<R$. Subtract $P(z)s_N(z)=0$ from step 4 and use the triangle inequality to obtain $1\le\sum_{k=0}^d |p_k||z|^k\sum_{n=N-k+1}^N b_n|z|^n$, where the inner sum is empty for $k=0$. Step 3 gives convergence of the real series $\sum_n b_n|z|^n$. For each fixed $k$ its displayed tail tends to zero, being a difference of two partial sums with the same limit. There are only finitely many $k$, so the right side tends to zero, contradicting $1\le0$. Thus $P(z)\ne0$ throughout the disc; this also covers $P=1$ and $z=0$.

lean.statement: theorem positive_product_radius {J : Type u} (f : J → ℂ⟦X⟧) (hf : ∀ j, (f j).HasNonnegCoeffs) (hconst : ∀ j, PowerSeries.constantCoeff (f j) = 1) (F : ℂ⟦X⟧) (hlocal : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ S : Finset J, (∀ (j : J) (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → PowerSeries.coeff k (f j) ≠ 0 → j ∈ S) ∧ PowerSeries.coeff n F = PowerSeries.coeff n (∏ j ∈ S, f j)) (R : ℝ≥0∞) (h : ℂ → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableOn ℂ h (Metric.eball 0 R)) (hTaylor : ∀ n : ℕ, PowerSeries.coeff n F = (Nat.factorial n : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv n h 0) : (∀ j : J, R ≤ (f j).radius) ∧ (∀ (j : J) (P : Polynomial ℂ), f j = (P : ℂ⟦X⟧)⁻¹ → P.eval 0 = 1 → ∀ z ∈ Metric.eball 0 R, P.eval z ≠ 0)
